classification.difficultyReason: Sketch solution curves, explain an isocline algebraically, verify it is a solution and interpret asymptotic behaviour.

content.prompt: The slope field for $y'=-\frac12x-y$ is shown.

spec.description: Equal-scale Cartesian axes with integer ticks −4 to 4, no zero label and no grid lines. Direction elements occur at every integer coordinate in the square −4 to 4.
spec.mathematics: Each direction element has gradient −x/2−y and constant length.
spec.answerVisibility: Axes, ticks and direction elements are permanent. Requested solution curves and isocline are omitted from the student graph.

answer.short: See the solution curves on the graph.
answer.worked: Through each given point, sketch a smooth curve tangent to the nearby line elements. The curve through $(-2,0)$ rises to a maximum and then falls; the curve through $(2,0)$ decreases. Both approach the straight isocline as $x$ increases.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Look at line elements on $x=1$, from bottom to top. Do gradients increase or decrease?

answer.worked: On $x=1$, $y'=-\frac12-y$. As $y$ increases from bottom to top, $y'$ decreases.

answer.short: The gradient is constant, $y'=-\frac12$, along the line.
answer.worked:
Substitute $y=\frac12-\frac12x$ into the differential equation:
$$\begin{aligned}y'&=-\frac{x}{2}-\left(\frac12-\frac{x}{2}\right)\\y'&=-\frac12.\end{aligned}$$
The gradient is constant along $y=\frac12-\frac12x$, so it is an isocline.

inlines.text: Show that this isocline is also a solution of the DE, then add it to your copy.

answer.short: Both sides equal $-\frac12$, so the line is a solution. See the dashed line on the graph.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\text{RHS}&=-\frac{x}{2}-\left(\frac12-\frac{x}{2}\right)\\&=-\frac12.\end{aligned}$$
$$\text{LHS}=y'=-\frac12\quad\text{(slope of the line).}$$
Therefore $y=\frac12-\frac12x$ is a solution of the DE. Add this straight line to the slope field.

children.label: e
children.prompt: What do you notice about the isocline and the two solution curves?

answer.short: The isocline is an asymptote for both solution curves.
answer.worked: Both solution curves approach $y=\frac12-\frac12x$ as $x$ increases, so this isocline is an asymptote for both.

spec.description: Complete answer graph with the two requested solution curves and the straight solution isocline, distinguished by a dashed stroke. All three retain continuation arrows.
spec.mathematics: Curves y=1/2−x/2−(3/2)e^{−(x+2)} and y=1/2−x/2+(1/2)e^{2−x} pass through (−2,0) and (2,0), respectively. The straight isocline is y=1/2−x/2.
